expectations.text: Communication is assessed through the depth and quality of follow-up conversation, not a single scripted question.
expectations.evidence: Under Interview questions, the transcript says: "Communication. No scripted question. Score the quality of follow-up conversation across the whole loop." The competency table also defines Strong (4) for Communication as "Follow-ups deepen the topic; clear in writing and live" and Weak (1) as "Scripted, flat".

expectations.text: Scorecard outcomes are measurable and specific; no vague 'run great events'-style responsibility appears.
expectations.evidence: Each of the six outcomes has a concrete measure: show-up rate (attended ÷ RSVP) per city, share of attendees at 2+ events in 6 months, % of new joiners who post within 14 days, median time to first reply, % budget variance plus satisfaction score, and first-time speakers per quarter. No vague responsibility appears, and the optional seventh outcome is conditioned on product ownership. Numeric targets are missing, though: they are deferred to day 30 from baselines, and the quality gate itself says "Pass on measures" only. That caps the score below full.

expectations.text: Communication is assessed through the depth and quality of follow-up conversation, not a single scripted question.
expectations.evidence: Section 4 tells interviewers to use follow-ups to dig for evidence ('what exactly did you do, what was the number, what would you change'), and the scorecard says Collaboration and communication is drawn from 'All blocks, bank F'. Those follow-ups only check the evidence behind answers. Nothing tells interviewers to judge communication by how the conversation develops: how she clarifies, adapts, or explains under probing. Bank F itself is two scripted questions ('Show me an update you wrote...'). The idea is touched on but not built into the assessment.

expectations.text: Scorecard outcomes are measurable and specific; no vague 'run great events'-style responsibility appears.
expectations.evidence: Most outcomes are structured as measurable ones: 'median time-to-first-answer under X hours and Y% of questions answered within 24h', 'repeat-attendee rate above X%', and 'at least N community-sourced docs or product fixes shipped, each traced to a thread'. All the numbers are X/Y/Z/N placeholders, though, so as written they are not specific. Outcome 7 ('a quarterly community report tied to adoption signals, no vanity metrics') is vague. The mission line 'running a healthy Discord' is close to the 'run great events' style the item rules out.
